title: Accelerated attention routing and dynamic clock-bound prefill scheduler for mixed-MIG SKUs
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: reduce 95th-percentile prefill+decode latency for mixed-SKU MIG fleets by combining attention-routing hints with a clock-bound prefill scheduler that adapts kernel selection and clock governors per-request.

Background: We have observed high latency variance on H100/L40S/A10 mixed clusters, especially under MIG fragmentation and burst workloads. Current scheduler selects kernels by static fingerprinting and applies global clock policies; this leads to suboptimal kernel choices and missed prefill windows, increasing tail latency for short queries and throttling throughput for dense-token multimodal requests.

Proposal: Implement an attention-routing hint layer that classifies requests into one of three runtime profiles (short-latency, throughput-latency-balanced, heavy-prefill) and exposes a small kernel-scoring vector to the kernel selector. Add a dynamic clock-bound prefill scheduler that temporarily raises per-slice clock targets for latency-critical short-latency requests if thermal headroom allows, otherwise re-routes to a compatible quantized kernel variant. The scheduler should consider MIG slice size, current thermal telemetry, NVLink topology, and per-slice active batch counts.

Deliverables:
- new attn-route service that emits kernel hints and profile labels
- scheduler patch to enforce transient clock targets and kernel fallbacks
- telemetry and dashboards for per-slice latencies and clock raises
- integration tests and a canary rollout plan
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile prefill+decode latency decreases by >=18% for short-latency profile on mixed H100/L40S/A10 testbed
Transient per-slice clock raises do not exceed thermal emergency thresholds and are rolled back automatically
Kernel selector uses attn-route hints when available and falls back safely when hints are absent
Canary on dedicated cluster shows no increase in token error rate or correctness regressions
Automated test coverage for scheduler decision boundaries and fallback paths
implementation_steps: Instrument existing runtime to surface attn fingerprints and per-request token density to attn-route
Prototype attn-route as Go microservice with model to classify three profiles (rule-based + lightweight ML)
Extend kernel selector API to accept kernel hints and scoring vector
Implement transient clock target API with autosanitization based on thermal telemetry
Add MIG-aware topology fetcher and NVLink-aware batch packing heuristics
End-to-end test on lab clusters: run synthetic short/long/throughput workloads and collect telemetry
Prepare canary plan and rollback criteria; coordinate with infra for limited clock raise permissions
telemetry_targets: number and duration of transient clock raises per hour
kernel hint hit rate and fallback rate
thermal headroom events and emergency rollbacks
notes: Trade-offs: transient clock raises help tail latency but consume headroom and may reduce energy efficiency. We will limit raises to short windows (<=200ms) and require explicit opt-in via canary.
Fallback strategy prioritized to preserve correctness: if kernel hint leads to missing KW in kernel cache or incompatible quantization, fallback to verified decode path.
Security: clock control requires infra privileges; will coordinate with infra and SRE to gate via service account and audit logs.
Benchmarks should include a mix of real customer prompts to detect output regressions.
